node.label: François Hartog
node.date_label: Le Miroir d’Hérodote (1980) · Régimes d’historicité (2003) · Anciens, Modernes, Sauvages (2005)
node.description: A historian of historiography whose regimes of historicity ask how past, present and future are articulated. His interviews describe presentism as a heuristic diagnosis and relate it to earlier anthropological questions about different ways of producing history.

incident_edges.relationship: Offers regimes of historicity as a heuristic for varying relations among past, present and future.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own ENS answer defines an instrument of inquiry rather than universal stages every society must pass through.

incident_edges.relationship: Diagnoses presentism as a shifting dominance of the present in relations to past and future.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own ENS explanation links diagnosis to observing discordant times after the Berlin Wall; not a claim historical time literally stopped.
